Chapter Six: The Ongoing Process—Growing Together Through Change.
Change—it's just part of life, isn't it? No matter how carefully you and your partner map out your future, the world always seems to have its own ideas. Maybe it's a new job in a different city. Maybe a baby arrives, or health throws you for a loop. Sometimes, dreams take new shapes.
And in a marriage, those changes don’t just happen to each person—they happen to both of you, together. Suddenly, the road ahead isn't as clear as it once seemed. You might find yourselves in unfamiliar territory, wondering, “Okay... how do we move forward from here?”
Picture this: It's a quiet morning. One of you is sitting at the kitchen table, staring at a letter that could change everything—maybe a surprise job offer, or some unexpected news from the doctor. The other walks in, senses the tension in the air, and sits down. The two of you talk—sometimes going in circles, sometimes just sitting in silence.
Of course, there's fear. But there’s also a strange spark of possibility. In these moments, your old ways of handling things might not fit anymore. You have to learn how to adapt—as a team.
I think a lot of people don’t realize how much marriage is about growing *together*, not just living side by side. It’s easy to drift apart when life gets hard. Maybe you start retreating into your own worlds. But the couples who make it through change are the ones who keep reaching for each other—even when it feels awkward or uncomfortable.
They ask new questions. They listen in new ways. They even let themselves be changed by what their partner is going through.
Sometimes, real growth means letting go of old dreams to make room for new ones. Other times, it’s about rediscovering each other after years of just getting through the routine. There’s a certain humility involved—a willingness to admit, “I’m not totally sure who you’re becoming, but I want to find out.”
That kind of openness? It’s what keeps a marriage alive, even when everything else is changing.
Over time, you start to see that marriage isn’t some fixed state. It’s a living, breathing process. The people who started out together aren’t exactly the same as the ones continuing the journey. And honestly, that’s a good thing.
The real miracle isn’t that two people stay the same, but that they keep choosing each other—again and again—no matter what changes life brings.
